text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malaysia wants Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew to retract statement on Johor Bahru being unsafe and tender an apology.
- National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University to raise enrollment of engineering students.
- At least two soccer players and one club official among 11 questioned by Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau regarding S-League matches.
- United Overseas Bank group companies and Hong Kong property group Parkview make top bids for two commercial plots.
- Paging subscribers who switch operators next month will not be charged extra for retaining existing numbers.
- Singapore's electronics industry output suffers fall of 10.9 percent in January.
- All listed companies on the mainboard may be required to have internal audit departments.
- Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang announces attractive budget for middle-income class and higher social spending but nothing for business community.
- Transport operator CityCab to supplement its fleet of Mercedes-Benz cabs.
- Government of Singapore Investment Corporation invests Singapore $50 million in Thai property market.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore eases disclosure rules on company directors' remuneration packages.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore is unlikely to shorten settlement period for share trading by end of this month.
- Motor-driven Cycle & Carriage Ltd announces net earnings of Singapore $200.1 million, up 10.2 percent.
- Hong Kong-based Noble Group's initial public offer is 18.8 times subscribed for 6.09 million shares at U.S. $0.88 each.
